I've actually not seen this topic come up much on Voat, but I have been involved in quite a few discussions on the topic in other venues. I think the biggest issue is actually that most people rely on headlines and fail to actually read underlying studies and information.

This wasn't a bad study and its conclusions actually sound about right if you delve into the details. However, it is highly misleading to summarize the findings of the study by saying more money doesn't increase happiness above $75k because that is NOT what the study actually found.

The study actually looked at two different types of happiness (I forget exactly what it called them). One was essentially your day to day comfort happiness level. The other was your longer term satisfaction with life happiness level.

The first does seem to cap out with earners making about $75k. They can buy the clothes they need. The car they need. Live in safe neighborhoods. Eat what they want. Et cetera. It makes sense. Think about your average day. You wake up, shower, go to work, eat lunch, work some more and go home for dinner. As long as you do not run into major problems, you are going to be about as happy with your day if you are making $75k or $300k.

You will not be nearly as happy if you are making $25k, because a lot of those simple simple things are stressful. Your car might break down on the way to work because it has been making a funny sound lately. You can't afford to buy lunch but you are out of sliced ham and bread. Et cetera.

On the issue of overall life happiness, the satisfaction level keeps growing the more you make. Someone contemplating what they want to do for vacation this year and how comfortable their retirement will be much happier if they are making $300k than those making $75k.

I can say from personal experience that going from $20K to $100K income has made me immensely happier.
